ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a common-emitter amplifier circuit. The signal source Us on the left is connected through the source resistor Rs and coupling capacitor C1 to the input bias node; above this node it is connected through RB1 to +12V, below it is connected through RB2 to the bottom line/ground, and at the same time it is connected through a resistor labeled RB3 to the transistor base. The transistor collector is connected through Rc to +12V, and is coupled through C2 to the load RL on the right; the emitter is connected to RE, while CE is connected in parallel with RE to ground. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, C1, C2, and CE can be regarded as short circuits for AC signals, therefore CE grounds the emitter for AC. When redrawing the AC input side according to the specified method, the input signal needs to pass through RB3 to the transistor base, and then sees the transistor small-signal input resistance rbe. Therefore the transistor input branch is equivalent to RB3 and rbe in series. Substituting RB3 = 0.5 kΩ and rbe = 1.5 kΩ gives Ri = RB3 + rbe = 0.5 + 1.5 = 2 kΩ.
